sentences.text: This creature featured two lines of bony plates along its back and additional plates on its belly.
Unlike most relatives, its fourth finger extended further than the middle digits.
Teeth stretched all the way to the snout's end, contradicting ideas that similar animals had beaks.
Remains were uncovered in the 1960s, marking the first find of an aetosaur in the Los Colorados Formation.
Biomechanical studies suggest Neoaetosauroides had a diet that diverged greatly from that of most other aetosaurs.
Its jaws were somewhat weaker but faster than those of other aetosaurs.
Researchers proposed that Neoaetosauroides may have eaten a generalized diet of soft-bodied colonial insects and small vertebrates.
Neoaetosauroides belongs to the subfamily Desmatosuchinae and the family Stagonolepididae.
Fossils of Neoaetosauroides date to the Norian age of the Late Triassic and were found in the Los Colorados Formation in La Rioja, Argentina.
Neoaetosauroides lived during the Norian stage, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
